dandiset_name: MC_Maze_Small: macaque primary motor and dorsal premotor cortex spiking activity during delayed reaching
citation: Churchland, Mark; Kaufman, Matthew (2022) MC_Maze_Small: macaque primary motor and dorsal premotor cortex spiking activity during delayed reaching (Version 0.220113.0408) [Data set]. DANDI Archive. https://doi.org/10.48324/dandi.000140/0.220113.0408

asset_used.identical_across_versions: same asset_id/blob/digest in both draft and published version 0.220113.0408
asset_used.verified_by: sha256sum of downloaded file in examples/bci/data/, matches digest returned by DANDI asset API

asset_not_used.reason: spiking-only release of the dataset's held-out test split with no published behavior/target labels; cannot be used for supervised quadrant labels, so prepare.py never downloads it

subject_session: single macaque (sub-Jenkins), single session ('small' maze). One subject/session: these results are NOT evidence of cross-day or cross-subject stability.
approach: electrophysiological approach (Utah-array-style ephys electrode recording), primary motor and dorsal premotor cortex

local_trial_split.note: this is the dataset's OWN published train/val partition stored in the NWB intervals/trials/split field, not a split we chose

usage_note: Offline, retrospective reach-quadrant classification from a public macaque ephys dataset. No human subjects, no clinical application, no causal/implant claims; this is decompiler weight-interpretability work, not a BCI control system.
